newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Kim to meet opposition over labour law.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Kim to meet opposition over labour law.

text.p: In a major reversal, South Korean President Kim Young-sam will meet opposition leaders to discuss a crisis over a controversial new labour law, state television said on Monday.
Kim has previously ruled out such a meeting.
An official at the presidential Blue House could not immediately confirm the report.

South Korean unionists returned to work on Monday after strike leaders called off indefinite stoppages. It was the first day of normal production since strikes began on December 26 after passage of the law that makes it easier for companies to lay off workers.

Kim has insisted he will neither scrap the law nor revise it. However, he has been meeting religious leaders, including the heads of the powerful Roman Catholic and Protestant churches, to try to seek a peaceful solution.
Opposition parties have been adamant that the law, rammed through parliament in a dawn session of ruling party deputies, must be scrapped.
